position changes get treated as information rather   than noise and billionaire Stanley Ducken Miller 
is one of them. And last month his family office   filed its quarterly disclosure with the SEC. 
Broadcom, Intel and Micron gone, liquidated   entirely. But in that same filing, there was a new 
2.94 million share stake in a company whose only   business is accumulating and staking Hyperlid's 
Hype token. Now, unless you've been living under   a rock, you've noticed that the entire market is 
arguing non-stop about whether the AI trade is a   bubble. But while everyone argues, the money has 
already started moving. That is what the beginning   of a rotation looks like. And based on the numbers 
that we're looking at, it's going to be a big one.   So, let's break down why the AI trade has gone 
a bit choppy rather than broken, where liquidity   goes when a 2-year trade stalls, and which 
corner of crypto the smart money is rotating   into. Because it isn't just Bitcoin. My name is 
Lewis, and this is the Coin Bureau. Despite a   lot of scrutiny, the AI trade is not collapsing. 
However, it's fair to say that at this juncture,   it's a bit tired. And in markets, those are very 
different. Look at what happened last month when   Nvidia reported earnings. Revenue came in at 
$96 billion, beating consensus by over 4% with   earnings per share of $2.22, beating by over 6% 
and management guiding it to 70% revenue growth   for the following fiscal year. An absolutely huge 
quarter for an already massive company, but over   the trailing month, the stock managed a gain 
of 2.8%. Then there's Broadcom, which reported   earlier this month. Revenue up 86% yearonear. AI 
semiconductor revenue up 221% to 16.7 billion.   and the CEO raising multi-year guidance to $230 
billion of AI revenue by 2028. Then its shares   fell after the print and over the trailing 
month, the stock is down over 16%. And that   tells you everything that you need to know about 
the market's appetite. When a trade is healthy,   good news moves prices. When a trade is exhausted, 
good news is already in the price and the only   thing left to trade is disappointment. And the 
positioning data backs up this idea. In July,   Bank of America's Global Fund Manager survey had 
82% of respondents calling long semiconductors   the most crowded trade on the planet, a record. By 
August, that had fallen to 53%. Roughly a third of   the most consensus trade in the world stepped back 
within a single month. So where did they go? Well,   money that has spent 2 years in one trade does 
not go to cash when that trade stalls. Cash is   a decision in and of itself. And allocators who've 
been paid handsomely for owning volatility did not   suddenly develop a taste for 4.7% in treasuries. 
What they do instead is look for the next asset   that offers a similar volatility profile with a 
more compelling story for the moment. And that   list is very, very short. You need something 
liquid enough to absorb size, volatile enough   to matter to performance, and early enough in its 
narrative that you aren't the last buyer. There's   one asset class that ticks all three boxes, and 
you could see it in market activity already.   As I make this video, over the past month, the 
NASDAQ 100 is down 0.6%, the S&P 500 is down 0.5%,   and the tech sector as a whole is down 0.3%. 
Over that same window, Bitcoin is up over 21%.   Ethereum is up 30%. Coinbase stock is up 20% and 
Hype is up 53%. That's all the proof of rotation   anyone needs. But of course, tracking money as it 
moves between asset classes like this is a tricky   task and requires a ton of time, which is why our 
research team does it full-time so that you don't   have to. And you can get all of their insight 
right here on YouTube just by joining the Coin   Bureau Club Light Plan. You'll get daily coverage 
across both crypto and traditional markets. Our   teams read on where the capital is going and 
none of the noise. And if you sign up today, your   first month is absolutely free. Just tap that join 
button below this video to get started. Now, back   to those receipts. After all, a rotation thesis is 
worthless without evidence, and the evidence here   is clear as day. That brings us to the big man, 
Draen Miller. His filings showed a position worth   $23 million in Hyperlquid Strategies. The same 
filing showed a new $64 million stake in Biter,   a Bitcoin miner turned data center operator, plus 
expanded positions in Riot, Hut 8, and Iron. He   wasn't alone in Biter either. Black Rockck, State 
Street, Citadel, Jane Street, Morgan Stanley,   and Invesco all disclosed positions in the 
company that quarter. And in just three months,   the number of institutional holders in Bitier 
jumped 122% to 202. Then we have the fund flows.   In the week ending the 4th of September, US 
spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled in $986 million,   a third consecutive week of inflows, taking 
the 3-week total to roughly 3.8 billion, the   strongest stretch of 2026. August brought in over 
3.5 billion, the biggest month since September   2025. And the 3rd of September saw a single day 
intake of 730 million. Ethereum ETFs added 1.85   85 billion across August, their best month in a 
year. And the Hype ETFs, which barely existed a   few months ago, have taken in 356 million 
since launch across five straight weeks of   inflows. So why might the hyperlquid position 
matter more than the Bitcoin numbers? Well,   because of what was actually bought. We're 
not talking about a macro allocator that just   wandered into a memecoin here. He bought equity 
in a company that held 29.3 million hype tokens,   then worth roughly 1.9 billion. A business that's 
generating staking revenue and running buybacks   of its own shares. And the protocol at the center
